blogs.title: Demystifying Direct Preference Optimization (DPO): The Zero‑RL Revolution in Language Model Fine‑Tuning
blogs.description: A deep dive into DPO’s core idea: replacing the two‑step reward‑model–RL pipeline with a single, closed‑form policy update. The post explains the mathematical relationship between KL‑constrained rewards and optimal policies, shows how a log‑ratio trick turns an RL objective into a simple binary cross‑entropy loss, and highlights why this makes training far more stable and computationally cheap.

blogs.title: From Preferences to Performance: Why DPO Beats PPO on Sentiment Control and Summarization
blogs.description: An accessible comparison of experimental results, focusing on the reward–KL trade‑off frontier. Readers will see how DPO consistently achieves higher reward with lower divergence from the reference model, outperforms PPO even when PPO has oracle rewards, and delivers better sentiment‑controlled generations and TL;DR summaries—all with minimal hyper‑parameter tuning.

blogs.title: Concrete Guided Example: Fine‑Tuning a 6B GPT with Direct Preference Optimization
blogs.description: Step‑by‑step walkthrough of a real training recipe: generating preference pairs, initializing the reference policy, choosing β, and running the DPO loss. The post includes code snippets, checkpoint files, and best practices for handling distribution shift and sampling temperatures. A perfect guide for researchers who want to replicate or extend the technique.

blogs.title: Why Your Language Model Is Already a Reward Model – The Theory Behind DPO
blogs.description: A non‑technical explanation of the key theorem that shows any reward function consistent with Bradley–Terry can be reparameterized using the model’s own log‐ratio to a reference policy. It discusses equivalence classes of rewards, KL constraints, and why this insight lets us sidestep explicit reward learning while guaranteeing optimality.

blogs.title: Practical FAQ: When to Use DPO, When Not to – Common Pitfalls & Gotchas
blogs.description: A quick‑start cheat sheet that covers common questions like “Can I use DPO without a SFT base?”, “What if my preference data comes from noisy annotators?”, “How do I set β?”, and “How does DPO scale to larger models?”. Each answer is backed by empirical observations from the paper’s experiments.
